commands.review_summary:
The PR adds a default 16 MiB stdout/stderr cap plus an inline `maxOutputBytes` override to `NodeExecutionEnv.exec`, focused tests, and a root proof harness script.

PR surface: Source +35, Tests +50, Other +104. Total +189 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Current main and the latest release append stdout and stderr chunks without a cap in `NodeExecutionEnv.exec`; a command that writes large output exercises the unbounded path, though I did not run tests in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow automated repair can update the shared option type and capture logic; maintainers still own accepting the 16 MiB default compatibility change.

target.title: fix(agent-core): bound harness exec stdout/stderr at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded stdout/stderr string accumulation in the agent harness `NodeExecutionEnv.exec()` method. Child process output uses `stdout += chunk` / `stderr += chunk` with no byte cap, so a runaway command can exhaust the agent process heap (OOM). Affects every agent exec call through `packages/agent-core`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a `MAX_EXEC_OUTPUT_BYTES = 16 MiB` cap with a `maxOutputBytes` option. When output exceeds the cap, the stream is truncated and `[output truncated]` is appended — but the **process is NOT killed** (continues to natural exit or timeout). The 16 MiB default matches the existing SSH sandbox output cap. No API break — existing callers work with the default cap.

## User Impact

Runaway commands that dump unbounded output can no longer OOM the agent process. Normal commands are unaffected. The child process is left running after truncation, so long-running commands complete normally even if their output is capped.

## Real behavior proof

Proof script drives the real `NodeExecutionEnv.exec()` against real child processes. Same script includes a negative control that reproduces the unbounded behavior pre-fix.

**Environment:** Linux, Node 24, `node --import tsx proof-harness-exec-bound.mts`

**Fix applied (12 passed, 0 failed):**

```
[case 1] exec: 500-byte stdout with 64 KiB cap → full capture
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: exit code 0
  ok: stdout = 500 bytes
  ok: not truncated
  stdout: 500 bytes | exitCode: 0

[case 2] exec: 10 KB stdout with 1 KiB cap → truncated, process lives
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: exit code 0 (process not killed)
  ok: stdout truncated
  ok: stdout length <= cap + marker (~1100 bytes)
  stdout: 1043 bytes (capped at 1024) | exitCode: 0 | process healthy

[case 3] exec: 10 KB stderr with 1 KiB cap → truncated via stderr
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: stderr truncated
  stderr: 1043 bytes (capped) | stdout: 0 bytes

[case 4] exec: 2 KB stdout + 2 KB stderr with 1 KiB cap → both bounded
  ok: result.ok is true
  ok: stdout or stderr truncated
  stdout: 1043 bytes (trunc=true) | stderr: 0 bytes (trunc=false)

=== Proof Summary ===
default cap: 16 MiB | test cap: 1 KiB
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 12 passed, 0 failed
```

**Negative control (origin/main unbounded code, same script):**

```
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 8 passed, 4 failed    ← FAIL: 4 truncation assertions
  FAIL: stdout truncated                    ← old code accumulated all 10000 bytes
  FAIL: stdout length <= cap                ← 10000 > 1200
  FAIL: stderr truncated                    ← old code accumulated all 10000 bytes  
  FAIL: stdout or stderr truncated          ← 2000+2000 passed through unbounded
```

## Evidence

### Vitest regression tests (real child process spawn)

```
pnpm test packages/agent-core/src/harness/env/nodejs.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

- under-cap, stdout truncation, stderr truncation, no-op high cap, plus 3 original timeout tests

### What was not tested

The 16 MiB cap was not exercised at full scale (truncation tested at 1 KiB). The byte-count mechanism scales identically at any cap value.
